---
title: "Letter to the editor"
format: html
editor: visual
---

Dear Editors,

We are pleased to submit our manuscript, "On the replicability of LLM-based linguistic annotation: Insights from close and extended replications of Morin & Marttinen Larsson (2025) using open-weight LLMs" for consideration for publication in *Linguistics Vanguard*. The original study, which was published in *Linguistics Vanguard*, relied on a commercial model by Anthropic (Claude Sonnet 3.5). In it, the authors presented "a replicable method for automating grammatical annotation". In addition to reporting on our replication attempts using publicly available open-weight models, we use our findings as a starting point for a broader discussion of how linguists can approach the use of LLMs in corpus annotation, addressing issues of accessibility, reproducibility, generalisability, and ethics.

We believe that this paper is important for several reasons. First, it addresses a timely and rapidly evolving topic – the use of LLMs in corpus annotation – with rigorous, empirically grounded evidence. Second, it contributes to ongoing conversations about reproducibility and replicability in (corpus) linguistics. Third, it offers practical guidance for linguists seeking to adopt LLM-based annotation methods, particularly regarding model choice, training procedures, and the importance of transparent reporting. In conducting this research, we followed Open Science practices throughout. We are happy to share our scripts, data, and materials alongside the manuscript to ensure full transparency and to facilitate further replication efforts.

We believe that *Linguistics Vanguard* is the ideal venue for this work. The journal has a demonstrated commitment to methodological innovation and to fostering dialogue on open and reproducible research practices. Our paper aligns closely with these values, and we hope it will be of interest to the journal's broad readership of linguists. Moreover, given that the original study was published in *Linguistics Vanguard*, we believe it is particularly fitting that our replication and discussion appear in the same venue, contributing to an ongoing scholarly conversation within your pages.

We would also like to suggest that, given the nature of our study, it would be appropriate to invite at least one of the authors of the original study to act as a reviewer. We did not contact the authors as part of this research, but we believe that it would be important to give them the opportunity to respond to our findings before publication. Naturally, we hope that a non-partial reviewer will also be invited to provide an independent assessment.

We thank you for considering our manuscript and look forward to hearing from you soon.

Best regards,

Elen Le Foll & Hannah Boxleitner
